package main

import (
	"context"
	"fmt"
	"sync"

	machine "github.com/whitaker-io/machine/v4"
)

// Order is the payload the end-to-end flow carries. Tags is a SLICE on purpose:
// it is what makes the tee's synthesized duplicator do real work.
type Order struct {
	ID   string
	Seen int
	Tags []string
}

// packetCount is how many data the TRANSPORT pushes. It is deliberately ONE
// FEWER than the count the token asserts: main pushes the remaining datum
// in-process through the exported ingest, so the token is reached only if that
// ingest actually delivered into the running graph. An ingest that is merely
// typed, or exported and never wired, leaves the flow one datum short.
const packetCount = 2

// Feed is the source transport. It pushes a fixed number of packets when the
// machine starts.
//
// IT MINTS DATA WITH machine.RebuildPacket, which is the exported packet
// constructor: there is no exported path from a Frame to a Packet, so this is the
// sanctioned way for a transport to produce one.
func Feed() machine.EdgeFactory[Order] {
	return func(node string, report machine.Report) (machine.Edge[Order], error) {
		return &feedEdge{node: node, ch: make(chan machine.Packet[Order], packetCount)}, nil
	}
}

type feedEdge struct {
	node string
	ch   chan machine.Packet[Order]
	once sync.Once
}

func (e *feedEdge) Start(ctx context.Context) error {
	e.once.Do(func() {
		for i := range packetCount {
			packet, err := machine.RebuildPacket(machine.FrameData{
				ID:     fmt.Sprintf("datum-%d", i),
				Source: e.node,
				Node:   e.node,
			}, Order{ID: fmt.Sprintf("order-%d", i), Tags: []string{"a"}})
			if err != nil {
				return
			}
			e.ch <- packet
		}
	})

	return nil
}

func (e *feedEdge) Send(ctx context.Context, packet machine.Packet[Order]) error {
	select {
	case e.ch <- packet:
		return nil
	case <-ctx.Done():
		return ctx.Err()
	}
}

func (e *feedEdge) Receive() <-chan machine.Packet[Order] { return e.ch }

func (e *feedEdge) Close() error { return nil }

// Interesting is the branch predicate. Everything is interesting, so every datum
// reaches the tee and the sink.
func Interesting(f machine.Frame[Order]) bool { return f.Value().ID != "" }

// Audit is the second sink, which consumes the tee's other branch.
func Audit(f machine.Frame[Order]) Order { return f.Value() }

// done is closed once the token has been printed, so main can exit on the datum
// rather than on a timer.
var done = make(chan struct{})

var emitOnce sync.Once

// Emit prints the LOCKED TOKEN from the fixture's own code. The harness asserts
// on the running program's stdout, so nothing but the flow actually driving data
// through can produce it.
func Emit(seen int) {
	emitOnce.Do(func() {
		fmt.Printf("flow-e2e: processed=%d\n", seen)
		close(done)
	})
}
